chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Sayf ibn 'Umaira, from Abi al-Maghra, from Sama'a, from Abi al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: Is everything in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) or do you have a say in it? He said: Rather, everything is in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
ai.seo_question: Are all Islamic rulings found exclusively in the Quran and Sunnah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the comprehensive nature of divine guidance is affirmed, establishing that every legal and practical matter has a ruling derived from the Quran and the Sunnah. This serves as a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence, countering the notion of independent juristic opinion (qawl) existing outside these two primary sources. It underscores the sufficiency of revelation for all aspects of religious and worldly affairs.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/-] al-Kafi: A number of our companions from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from Ismail b. Mihran from Sayf b. ‘Amira from Abi al-Maghra from Sama’a from Abi al-Hasan Musa عليه السلام, he said:

I said to him: is everything in the book of Allāh and the Sunna of his prophet صلى الله عليه وآله or do you have a say in it? he said: rather everything is in the book of Allāh and the Sunna of the prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
